final_claim.narrative:
No time-respecting cascade from 3027 to 2549 exists in [42400, 52000]. Direct test with the 600-unit relay constraint returns reached=false, expanding to only 2 nodes from the source (step_01), and no time-respecting route is enumerable (step_15).

The key point is that this is not a mere absence of connectivity. A complete static chain 3027->4358->7049->4149->3213->2549 exists, and every hop is present in the correct forward orientation (steps 10-14: each is u->v with zero reverse events). Ignoring time ordering entirely, 2549 still sits in the union of the two k-hop neighbourhoods (steps 05, 07). So the 'connection exists when time is ignored' explanation is satisfied yet the cascade still fails — the chain is broken purely by event ordering, not by missing edges.

Locating the break: with max_wait removed altogether, reachability still fails and expands to only 3 nodes, 3027/4358/7049 (step_04). This means 3027->4358 then 4358->7049 are correctly ordered but separated by more than 600 units (they are excluded under the constraint in step_01 but admitted without it), and the chain then dies at 7049: the 7049->4149 event must timestamp earlier than the arrival at 7049, so the downstream half of the path is unusable in any ordering. Confirming this, the downstream segment tested on its own from 7049 to 2549 also fails (step_16), so the break is not an artefact of the upstream delay.

Confounders ruled out: window truncation is not responsible — widening to [35000, 60000] still yields no cascade (step_08). Volume/popularity is not masking a signal either; the window holds 3209 events over 3500 active nodes with a near-zero repeat ratio of 0.0009 (step_02), and both endpoints are singletons with exactly one event and one partner each (step_03), so there is no dense background of repeated contacts that could supply an alternative timing. Conclusion: a static path exists, but temporal order forbids influence transfer.
